subject: Nanotechnology
title: Thermoelectric Nanomaterials
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Thermoelectric Nanomaterials.

hook.text: Waste heat is everywhere — thermoelectric nanomaterials turn temperature differences directly into electricity.

buildup.text: The Seebeck effect drives electrons from hot to cold — creating a voltage proportional to the temperature gradient.

discovery.text: Nanostructured bismuth telluride scatters phonons at grain boundaries — cutting thermal conductivity while preserving charge flow.

twist.text: The figure of merit ZT rarely exceeds 2.5 — converting more than a few percent of heat to electricity is still hard.

climax.text: Body-heat powered wearables use flexible nano thermoelectric films — skin warmth drives health monitoring sensors.

punchline.text: Nano-grain boundaries block heat but let electrons flow — waste heat becomes power.

quiz.question: How do nanostructured thermoelectrics improve efficiency?
options: They increase thermal conductivity to move heat faster
Grain boundaries scatter phonons, reducing thermal conductivity while maintaining electrical conductivity
They convert light to heat before generating electricity
